rules.title: Integer literals that exceed their type range are rejected
rules.statement: An integer literal whose value cannot be represented (would silently saturate/truncate) is a compile error: 'integer literal out of range'. ≤64-bit literals are bound-checked against i64/destination range; literals with u128/i128 suffix are bound-checked against the 128-bit range.

rules.title: Suffixed integer literal bound-checked against suffix type
rules.statement: A suffixed integer literal `Nsuf` is given type `suf` and its magnitude is bound-checked against that type's range: signed types permit |min| (e.g. i8 down to -128, up to 127), unsigned types permit 0..2^N-1. Exceeding the bound is 'integer literal out of range for its suffix type'.

rules.title: Leading unary minus folds into integer literal for range check
rules.statement: A leading unary minus is folded into the integer literal before range checking, so the magnitude is bounded by |min| rather than max (e.g. `-128i8` is valid, equal to i8::MIN).

rules.title: Negative value with unsigned suffix is rejected
rules.statement: A negative integer literal with an unsigned suffix (u8/u16/u32/u64/u128) is a compile error: 'negative value with unsigned suffix'.

rules.title: Unsuffixed integer literal has inferred-integer type
rules.statement: An integer literal without a suffix is given a polymorphic integer-literal type whose concrete type is resolved later by destination-type coercion; only suffixed literals get a fixed primitive type at lowering.

rules.title: Malformed integer literal is rejected
rules.statement: An integer literal whose textual form is not a valid integer literal is a compile error: 'malformed integer literal'.

rules.title: Character literal escape sequences
rules.statement: A char literal `'c'` accepts the escapes \n \t \r \0 \\ \' \" ; \xNN (exactly 2 hex digits, byte 0..255); and \u{H..} (1..6 hex digits in braces). Any other escape is a compile error.

rules.title: char value must be a valid Unicode scalar
rules.statement: A \u{H..} char value must be a Unicode scalar value: ≤ U+10FFFF and not in the surrogate range U+D800..U+DFFF; otherwise it is a compile error. A char literal lowers to a value of type `char`.

rules.title: Multibyte char literal body decoded as one UTF-8 codepoint
rules.statement: A char literal whose body is a single multibyte character is decoded as exactly one UTF-8 codepoint; a malformed or length-mismatched UTF-8 body is a compile error.

rules.title: Byte-string literal has type [u8; N]
rules.statement: A byte-string literal `b"…"` lowers to an array literal of type `[u8; N]` where N is the decoded byte count; it accepts the escapes \n \t \r \0 \\ \' \" and \xNN (2 hex digits). Unknown or malformed escapes are compile errors.

rules.title: Reference to an undefined name is an error
rules.statement: A variable reference whose name resolves to no local binding, const-generic parameter, function, enum variant, or unit struct is a compile error: 'undefined variable'.

rules.title: Const-generic parameter usable in value position
rules.statement: A const-generic parameter `<const N: T>` referenced in expression position evaluates to a value of its underlying numeric type T (default i64); monomorphization substitutes the concrete constant.

rules.title: Bare function name has a distinct per-function fn-item type
rules.statement: A function name used as a value has a zero-sized fn-item type unique to that function (distinct type per function/instantiation), which auto-coerces to the corresponding `fn(T)->R` pointer type at value-use sites.

rules.title: Unit struct name in value position constructs it
rules.statement: A bare name of a known zero-field, non-generic struct in value position constructs that struct (unit-struct construction); a fielded struct still requires `S { … }` form.

rules.title: Imported no-payload enum variant usable as a bareword
rules.statement: A no-payload enum variant brought into scope via `use Type.{V, …};` (or the prelude bareword `None`) can be referenced as a bare identifier, constructing that variant; payload-carrying variants require call syntax.

rules.title: Use of a moved variable is an error
rules.statement: Reading a variable after its value has been moved out is a compile error: 'use of moved variable'.

rules.title: Use of a possibly-uninitialised binding is an error
rules.statement: Reading a binding declared without an initializer (`let x: T;`) before a definite assignment on the current path is a compile error (Rust E0381); at if/match merge points a binding is uninitialised if uninitialised on any incoming path.

rules.title: Reading a mutable static requires unsafe
rules.statement: Reading a `static mut` outside an `unsafe` block is a compile error (Rust items.static.mut.safety); the gate is suppressed when the name is shadowed by a local binding or a const-generic parameter.

rules.title: Accessing an extern static requires unsafe
rules.statement: Any access to an extern static outside an `unsafe` block is a compile error (Rust items.extern.static), with the same local/const-param shadowing suppression as mutable statics.

rules.title: Deref coercion through user/stdlib Deref(Mut) impls
rules.statement: A receiver of struct type with a Deref/DerefMut impl deref-coerces by calling `deref`/`deref_mut` to obtain `&Target`; for an unsized Target (dyn or slice) the returned fat reference is the value itself with no further place-deref. A mutable deref step may fall back to the Deref Target when only Deref is implemented (shared supertrait Target).

rules.title: Deref impl selected by strict self-type match among multiple impls
rules.statement: When a type carries several Deref impls distinguished by self type-args (e.g. Pin<&T>/Pin<&mut T>/Pin<Box<T>>), the impl whose target pattern strictly unifies-substitutes-and-equals the receiver type is selected; a non-matching impl is used only as a loose fallback.

rules.title: Droppable rvalue auto-ref receiver lives to end of statement
rules.statement: A fresh owning (move-type) rvalue receiver auto-referenced to `&self`/`&mut self` is hoisted into the enclosing statement's block as a named local so it lives to end-of-statement and is then dropped by scope exit, matching Rust temporary-scope semantics; non-droppable or place/borrow receivers keep a plain temp spill.
